column1: Kth Largest Element in an Array — given int array `nums` and integer k, return the kth LARGEST element. Example: [3,2,1,5,6,4], k=2 → 5; [3,2,3,1,2,4,5,5,6], k=4 → 4.
column2: PATTERN: Min-heap of size k (or quickselect). | INSIGHT: Maintain a min-heap of the k largest seen so far; the root is the kth largest. | STEPS: 1) heap=[]. 2) For x in nums: heappush(heap,x); if len(heap)>k: heappop(heap). 3) Return heap[0]. | TIME/SPACE: O(n log k) / O(k). | PITFALL: Quickselect gives O(n) average but is harder to write under interview pressure.

column1: IPO — given k projects with `capital[i]` and `profit[i]`, starting capital w; pick at most k projects (one at a time, sequentially), each adds its profit to capital. Maximize final capital. Example: k=2, w=0, profits=[1,2,3], capital=[0,1,1] → 4 (start 0; pick profit 1 → cap 1; pick profit 3 → cap 4).
column2: PATTERN: Two heaps — min-heap by capital (waiting), max-heap by profit (available). | INSIGHT: At each step, move all projects with capital ≤ w from waiting to available; pick the max-profit one. | STEPS: 1) Sort projects by capital. 2) For _ in range(k): while sorted projects have capital<=w: push profit to max-heap. If max-heap empty: break. w += -heappop(max_heap). 3) Return w. | TIME/SPACE: O(n log n) / O(n). | PITFALL: Python heapq is min-only — negate values to simulate max-heap.

column1: Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums — given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` and integer k; return k pairs (u,v) with u from nums1, v from nums2, having the smallest sums. Example: nums1=[1,7,11], nums2=[2,4,6], k=3 → [[1,2],[1,4],[1,6]].
column2: PATTERN: Min-heap with index pairs and dedup trick. | INSIGHT: Start with (sum,0,0); on pop, push neighbors (i,j+1) and conditionally (i+1,0) — only when j==0 — to avoid duplicates. | STEPS: 1) heap=[(nums1[0]+nums2[0], 0, 0)]; ans=[]. 2) While heap and len(ans)<k: s,i,j=heappop. ans.append([nums1[i],nums2[j]]). If j+1<len(nums2): push (nums1[i]+nums2[j+1], i, j+1). If j==0 and i+1<len(nums1): push (nums1[i+1]+nums2[0], i+1, 0). 3) Return ans. | TIME/SPACE: O(k log k) / O(k). | PITFALL: Without the j==0 dedup trick, you'd add the same cell multiple times.

column1: Find Median from Data Stream — design a class with addNum(num) and findMedian() supporting streaming insertion. Example: addNum(1); addNum(2); findMedian()→1.5; addNum(3); findMedian()→2.0.
column2: PATTERN: Two heaps — max-heap (low half) + min-heap (high half), kept balanced. | INSIGHT: Keep |low| ≥ |high|, differing by 0 or 1. Median = low.top (odd total) or avg of tops (even). | STEPS: addNum(v): 1) heappush(low, -v). 2) heappush(high, -heappop(low)) (move max of low to high). 3) If len(high)>len(low): heappush(low, -heappop(high)). findMedian: if len(low)>len(high): -low[0]; else (-low[0]+high[0])/2. | TIME/SPACE: O(log n) add, O(1) median / O(n). | PITFALL: Always-push-to-low-then-rebalance is the cleanest pattern.
